testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with dual air brake systems?

options.text: They keep full air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
They keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
The engine must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
They do not need time to build air pressure before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving, you must let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi of air pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: While driving downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until your speed drops 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how long should it take air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for the air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This should take about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When traveling down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking power.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking power.
questions.explanation: The engine's braking power should be your main way to control speed going downhill. Shift down before the hill and use brakes only when needed for extra slowing or stopping.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob to set the parking brake and push it in to release it.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: It is important to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch that:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light
Turns off the low pressure warning light

questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing the brake pedal sends air pressure to an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn the parking brake on and off
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times
Disconnect and reconnect all glad hands

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times
questions.explanation: After the system is charged, test the warning signal by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air and the warning light should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver gradually apply spring brakes. It is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system use the same air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking up
Stop a vehicle from speeding up while going uphill
Stop a vehicle from speeding up while going downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: On trucks and buses, where is the ABS warning light?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle near the passenger door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with anti-lock brakes have a yellow warning light on the dashboard. Trailers have a yellow warning light on the left side, either on the front or back corner.

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove oil and water that build up in the tanks. They can be opened by hand or automatically.

questions.question: What color is the ABS warning light?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock brakes have yellow warning lights.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that spring brakes turn on automatically when:
questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure spring brakes engage when air pressure falls between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and press the brake pedal to release air. The parking brake should pop out and spring brakes should engage when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes
A part that allows air to flow freely in the brakes

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:
questions.explanation: Before going downhill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster on the hill.

questions.question: A dual air brake system has:

options.text: One air brake system but two sets of controls
One air brake system for each side of the truck
Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls. One system controls the rear axle brakes. The other system controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valves were made to:

options.text: Keep the front tires from skidding
Keep the front tires from overheating
Use front and rear brakes equally

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front tires from skidding
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves to reduce front wheel skidding. However, research shows these are not needed, so they should stay in the "normal" position.

questions.question: Test the low pressure warning light:
questions.explanation: Test your low pressure warning light before each trip. Let the system fill with air, then press and release the brake pedal quickly to release air. The warning light should come on when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Brakes can go out of adjustment if:
questions.explanation: Brakes can go out of adjustment quickly when they overheat from use. Check your brake adjustment often.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system brakes different axles.

questions.question: A vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to show the system is not working.
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS fails, you can still use your regular brakes.

questions.question: Which of the following is not part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.
Open the door to the cab.

questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both spring pressure and air pressure together can damage the brakes.
